The headwaters of the Yazoo River near Greenwood
Aerial photo: USDA NAIP, available from U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program

Source & image record ↗ · Public domain · The National Map

This modern river landscape shows the junction of the Tallahatchie and Yalobusha near Greenwood. The Fort St. Pierre nomination places Chakchiuma history in this part of the upper Yazoo region. The image is resized for the web.

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Names in colonial records and relationships with Chickasaw and Choctaw histories. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] chickasawculturalcenter.com [2] chickasaw.net [3] thechickasawvillages.com

03

Chakchiuma in the upper Yazoo region

The Fort St. Pierre nomination discusses the Chakchiuma in the upper Yazoo and Yalobusha River region. Karl G. Lorenz explains how earlier Spanish accounts are interpreted in relation to the Chakchiuma name.

Read the sources [4] National Park Service, National Historic Landmarks Program [5] Mississippi Encyclopedia / Center for the Study of Southern Culture

Sources for map connections

  • Mississippi · Historical tribal group geography in specialist reference

    The article explicitly identifies Sacchuma with Chakchiuma among historic tribal groups in Mississippi named in the Spanish accounts. This supports a Mississippi historical connection while attributing the correspondence to the encyclopedia interpretation.

    • Mississippi Encyclopedia — Protohistoric Period
